messages:
jess: Quick convo starter — we need a durable resume token design that survives model/region fallback. current opaque blob is fine but servers change shape and SDKs explode.

omar: Agreed. Two patterns we tested: (1) single opaque blob with a stable envelope (prefix+base64) + optional human debug; (2) thin session descriptor object returned by a control-plane call and referenced by id in subsequent calls.

lee: Pattern (2) is cleaner for operator-inspection but requires server sticky state (session store) and hurts long-lived tokens for offline clients.

sam: Can we hybridize? short-lived session-id for active streams + long-lived opaque token for passive pagination / resume across restarts. server can exchange between them.

jess: Exactly. Proposal: resume token = prefix + base64(envelope). envelope fields: ver, kind, seq, shard, chk, dbg. keep semantics transport-agnostic (no HTTP/gRPC specifics). servers can map to session-id internally.

lee: Example envelope JSON (not the token itself):
```json
{"ver":2, "kind":"pager", "seq":4321, "shard":"r2", "chk":"f7a9", "dbg":"zone=eu;model=gpt-medium"}
```
Encoded with prefix: `sess2:` + base64(envelope).

omar: For retries we need an SDK Policy object with: max_retries, backoff (strategy name + base_ms), idempotency (safe/unsafe/unsafe-with-hints). SDK maps to transport retry headers and non-idempotent endpoints get stricter defaults.

sam: Language ergonomics: TS -> AsyncIterable pager; Python -> async generator + sync helper .sync_iter(); Go -> function returning (<-chan Item, cancel func). Keep a shared Pager interface in spec and provide adapters.

jess: Edge cases: token version mismatch. server responds with TOKEN_VERSION_MISMATCH + recommended minimum client version and link. SDKs should surface a specific error type and optionally auto-fetch a fresh token (if server supports token-exchange endpoint).

lee: Debugability: include short human debug field in envelope but keep full decode optional. support toolchain: sdk debug flag => sdk logs base64 decode + pretty json (only when enabled).

omar: Security: don't put PII in dbg. mark tokens short-lived if they contain sensitive routing hints. recommend servers scrub sensitive fields when handing to clients.

sam: Tests: need cross-lang matrix for resume semantics when fallback occurs (model downgrades mid-stream, region failover). create test harness that simulates: drop, model-fallback, token-incompatibility.

jess: Ops automation: @ops-bot queue a compatibility job after RFC lands. will also include a migration plan: v1 tokens continue to be accepted for N months with a warning code on decode.

ops-bot: Job 'resume-token-compat-matrix' created and queued for execution.

omar: Next steps: I will draft the token envelope schema + policy shape. @lee please add language adapter signatures. sam will write the test matrix. jess will own RFC writeup and rollout plan.

jess: Thanks. keep defaults conservative: low retries for non-idempotent, clear errors for unsupported token, and debug opt-in only.

lee: I'll sketch the TS/py/go examples and drop them in the RFC PR.

sam: lgtm, will follow up with CI jobs. :+1:
